messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, mobile-friendly 2D Pokémon collection game about finding Pokémon by luck.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for visual checks, at viewport width no more than 1280px.

## Decisions
- Built a responsive browser game called “Pocket Trails” with habitat-based random encounters, Poké Ball capture chances, berries, energy, a Pokédex, daily tasks, and persistent local saves.
- Used emoji artwork and CSS-drawn scenery rather than external Pokémon art assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `app.js` for the game interface and mechanics.
- Verified `node --check app.js` and exercised searching, catching a Pokémon, and browsing the Pokédex in Playwright.
- Captured and inspected `/tmp/opencode/pocket.jpg` at 430px viewport width.

### Active
- Fix the duplicate Pokédex number: Eevee is currently assigned ID `133`, duplicating Snorlax; Eevee should be `133` and Snorlax should retain `143` (the current species data has Snorlax `133`, Eevee `133`, and Dratini `147`).
- Consider doing a final pass on game UI and mechanics after correcting the species IDs.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Correct species IDs in `app.js` and confirm all 12 Pokédex entries have unique, accurate numbers.
2. Run `node --check app.js` and verify the Pokédex displays the corrected IDs.
3. Report the game complete and briefly note assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens, navigation, encounter dialog, and user-facing UI.
- `styles.css`: Responsive mobile/tablet styling, scenery, and animations.
- `app.js`: Pokémon data, local persistence, encounters, capture logic, Pokédex, tasks, and bag.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- A local server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`; Playwright is open at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Playwright showed one console error from a missing `/favicon.ico`; the game itself loaded and functioned.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, mobile-friendly 2D Pokémon game focused on chance-based encounters and collection.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for visual checks at viewport widths no greater than 1280px.

## Decisions
- Built “Pocket Trails,” a responsive browser game with habitat-based random encounters, Poké Ball capture, berries, energy, a Pokédex, field notes, and local saves.
- Used emoji artwork and CSS-drawn scenery instead of external Pokémon art.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game interface and mechanics in `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `app.js`.
- Corrected Pokédex species IDs: Eevee `133`, Snorlax `143`, Dratini `147`; verified all 12 IDs are unique.
- `node --check app.js` passes.
- Verified the Pokédex displays the corrected numbers in Playwright.
- Captured and inspected the mobile screenshot at `/tmp/opencode/pocket.jpg` (430px wide).

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Report the game as complete and briefly note the implementation assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens, navigation, encounter dialog, and UI.
- `styles.css`: Responsive styling, CSS-drawn scenery, and animations.
- `app.js`: Pokémon data, local persistence, encounters, capture logic, Pokédex, tasks, and bag.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- A local server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`; Playwright verified the app at `http://localhost:3002`.
- The earlier `/favicon.ico` 404 was observed; it did not prevent the game from loading or functioning.

content.text:
Implemented **Pocket Trails**, a responsive Pokémon collection game in `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `app.js`.

It includes habitat-based random encounters, Poké Ball capture, berries, energy, a Pokédex, field notes, and local saves. I used emoji artwork and CSS-drawn scenery rather than external Pokémon art. I also corrected and verified the species IDs, and `node --check app.js` passes.

The mobile layout was checked at 430px wide; its screenshot is saved at `/tmp/opencode/pocket.jpg`.
